explanation:
## The program

```cpp
int hours{ s / 3600 };
int leftover{ s % 3600 };
int minutes{ leftover / 60 };
int seconds{ leftover % 60 };

std::cout << hours << ':';
if (minutes < 10) std::cout << '0';
std::cout << minutes << ':';
if (seconds < 10) std::cout << '0';
std::cout << seconds << "\n";
```

## Divide for the count, take the remainder for the rest

That is the whole idea, applied twice. `s / 3600` is "how many whole
hours are in `s`"; `s % 3600` is "and how much was not an hour". The
second number is a smaller version of the same problem, so the same
pair of operators solves it with 60 instead of 3600.

```
s = 3661

  3661 / 3600 = 1        hours    = 1
  3661 % 3600 = 61       leftover = 61
    61 /   60 = 1        minutes  = 1
    61 %   60 = 1        seconds  = 1
```

Written without the intermediate variable, minutes is `s / 60 % 60`.
That reads left to right — divide by 60 to get total minutes, then
take 60 of them away at a time — and it is correct, but `leftover`
makes the structure visible, and you can print it while debugging.

## Why the hour is not wrapped

The problem asks for an elapsed time, not a time of day. 90061
seconds really is 25 hours and a bit; printing `1:01:01` would be
answering a different question, and it is the question a `% 24` would
quietly change it into. Only wrap a unit when the thing being
measured wraps.

## Padding without <iomanip>

The library way is:

```cpp
#include <iomanip>
std::cout << std::setw(2) << std::setfill('0') << minutes;
```

which is worth knowing and has a catch: `setw` applies to the next
item only, while `setfill` is sticky and stays set for everything
afterwards. Two `if`s have no such surprise, and on a two-digit pad
they are not longer.

## What this does not check

Negative input. The constraint says the number is not negative, and
the reference does not test for it — with a negative `s` every
division truncates towards zero and the output is nonsense rather
than an error. A program taking this from a user rather than from a
well-behaved test would have to say so.
